title: Hollow and Choir Anew
premise: Kestrel Thackeray, cartographer and ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, has spent a decade making herself unremarkable so no one from her past can find her. When a mute child arrives speaking the pre-kingdom tongue of the Hollow Choir, Kestrel recognizes it because she once spoke it too—before she bought her own survival by selling another's name to the court beneath the mountain. The child is that soul, returned to collect. To save them both, Kestrel must map the unmappable court, outwit its tithe-collecting magistrates, and choose between keeping her hidden identity and giving the child back her stolen name. In the end, Kestrel surrenders her own name to the court in exchange for the child's freedom, becoming a blank page—until the guild, ledgers open, writes her back into the world as someone new.
about_author: Quentin Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. Hollow and Choir Anew is their second novel, following the critically praised The Tithe of Small Hours.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Unremarkable Things
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. We meet her double life: cartographer by day, keeper of the Guild of Impossible Things' ledgers by night, each entry a small erasure of herself. A routine audit reveals an entry she never wrote—a debt dated ten years ago, marked PAID IN FULL. Emotional beat: unease beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. During a storm, a mud-caked girl of about eight appears at the guild door and speaks a language predating kingdoms. Kestrel understands every word—and answers before she can stop herself. The girl calls her by a name Kestrel buried a decade ago. Emotional beat: terror of being known.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buys
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Ovid Sarn's POV. Sarn recognizes the child as merchandise: souls sold to the court beneath the mountain sometimes walk back up, and they fetch fortunes. He orders the girl locked in the map vault 'for safekeeping.' Emotional beat: cold commerce masking fear of the court.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Blank Pages
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, flashback-woven. We learn how young Kestrel escaped the court's tithe by trading away her companion's name—her sister-figure Wren—in exchange for her own passage. She has been invisible ever since, on purpose. Emotional beat: guilt calcified into survival.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Speaks in Roots
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In the vault, Kestrel teaches the girl—whom she names Ash—enough common speech to learn the truth: Ash carries Wren's sold soul, sent back up as the court's final collection notice. Emotional beat: tenderness entangled with dread.

chapters.title: Magistrates at the Door
chapters.summary: Sarn's POV. Two tithe-magistrates arrive wearing faces like unfinished sketches, demanding the returned soul. Sarn stalls, offering ledgers instead. They accept—but leave a black seal on the guild door: three days until collection. Emotional beat: the illusion of safety cracking.

chapters.title: Mapping the Undermountain
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel begins drafting a map of the court beneath the mountain from half-memory, discovering her cartographer's gift works on places that refuse to exist. Each line she draws costs her a memory of her old life. Emotional beat: sacrifice made literal.

chapters.title: The Thief's Confession
chapters.summary: Ash's POV, rendered in her fragmenting new language. Ash remembers being Wren: the sale, the dark, the long climb back as something assembled from scraps. She does not blame Kestrel—yet—which is worse. Emotional beat: forgiveness that feels like accusation.

chapters.title: Ovid's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sarn's POV. Cornered by the guild's creditors, Sarn secretly offers Ash to the magistrates early in exchange for his own debts forgiven. Kestrel overhears through the ledger-room wall. Emotional beat: betrayal by the man who taught her invisibility.

chapters.title: Running the Stair That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Ash flee through the guild's unmapped corridors using Kestrel's half-finished map, pursued by sketch-faced bailiffs. The map rewrites itself around their choices. They escape into the city's forgotten undercrofts. Emotional beat: desperate, exhilarating flight.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot Its Own Name
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Hiding among the Nameless—people erased by the court who live in the undercity—Kestrel finds allies who remember her crime and, remarkably, don't condemn it. Their leader, a faceless woman called Mother Vellum, offers passage down the mountain. Emotional beat: grace from the unforgivable.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Mother Vellum's POV. The Nameless hold their own trials for those who sold names; Kestrel submits herself voluntarily. The verdict: guilty, but her sentence is the journey itself—she must go down and return what was taken or be unmade. Emotional beat: accountability chosen freely.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Ash descend the tithe-road, where the mountain eats sound and memory. Kestrel loses her mother's face, then her native language, paying tolls she cannot refuse. Ash grows stronger as Kestrel dims—their souls resonating. Emotional beat: love measured in loss.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. They reach the court: a cathedral of stacked ledgers where magistrates are former sellers who failed to pay. The Presiding Quill—an enormous hand writing eternally—acknowledges Kestrel's arrival with terrible courtesy. Emotional beat: awe curdled into horror.

chapters.title: Terms of Return
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel petitions for Wren's soul. The court agrees—but insists on equivalent payment: a name of equal weight, freely given. Kestrel realizes what it demands. Ash begs her not to. Emotional beat: the trap of fair bargains.

chapters.title: Wren, Whole
chapters.summary: Ash/Wren's POV. The court briefly restores Wren's full soul to negotiate, and for one hour Kestrel speaks with the person she betrayed. Wren refuses the exchange: 'I didn't climb back up to watch you disappear.' Emotional beat: reunion as reckoning.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Defying both Wren and the court, Kestrel signs her name into the great ledger. Her identity unravels page by page—her history, her craft, her self—while Wren's soul is released whole into Ash's body. Emotional beat: self-annihilation as the ultimate act of will.

chapters.title: Blank
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Ash wakes on the mountainside with Wren's memories restored, beside a woman who has no name, no past, and eyes full of quiet panic. The Nameless take them in. Ash begins telling the nameless woman stories of who she was. Emotional beat: grief and guardianship intertwined.

chapters.title: The Ledger Opens Both Ways
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Sarn's POV. Sarn, ruined and hunted by the magistrates he tried to appease, discovers the guild's master ledger now contains a blank entry bearing Kestrel's seal—one that can be written into. He must decide whether to restore her or erase himself. Emotional beat: a coward's chance at courage.

chapters.title: Written Back
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Sarn, Mother Vellum, and Wren jointly author a new entry—not restoring the old Kestrel but creating someone who chooses to exist: same hands, same gift, new name. The court's seal cracks as the ink dries. Emotional beat: community as resurrection.

chapters.title: Hollow, Choir Anew
chapters.summary: Newly named Kestrel's POV. The magistrates come for the escaped soul one last time and find the guild standing together, ledgers balanced, the debt discharged in full. The Presiding Quill, denied its tithe, closes the account forever. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, vigilantly kept.

chapters.title: Cartography of the Possible
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, epilogue. One year later: Kestrel teaches Ash—now Wren again—to draw maps of real places, while the guild quietly becomes a refuge for the erased. On the last page, Kestrel writes her own name in a ledger for the first time, freely. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed as choice, not inheritance.
